subject: Cyclone AI RFI: reservation SKU match, burst runway & SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cycloneai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cycloneai.com, RFP Team <rfp@cycloneai.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing + SLA questions

Hi Karthik and Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intake form earlier. Cyclone AI is evaluating reserved inference capacity for a multi-region rollout (US east + EU) and we need a detailed fitment Q&A to finalize internal procurement. Key asks we need answers to within the next 48 hours:

- Recommended GPU SKUs for a 200k qps equivalent steady-state (text-gen + embeddings mix) and expected token/sec per GPU by model family.
- Tail-latency budget (p95/p99) we can expect on those SKUs for sequence lengths up to 1024.
- Burst runway: how much burst (x baseline) can be accommodated without pre-warming, and what are the cold-start characteristics?
- Fallback behavior: if a selected SKU is unavailable, can requests transparently fall back to a compatible model/quantization variant?
- Pricing/commitment tiers and how burst capacity is billed.

We attached our high-level throughput profile and would appreciate a short workbook or matrix that maps SKUs to expected throughput and cost per 1M tokens.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Ops, Cyclone AI
(elena.rossi@cycloneai.com)

--
Cyclone AI procurement request attached: Cyclone_RFP_ReservedInference_20270519.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cycloneai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing + SLA questions

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a SKU matrix (preliminary) and a short note below that maps your profile to practical options. We can follow up with a 30-min workshop to validate traffic shape and finalize the reservation runway.

Summary answers (short):
- Recommended SKUs: For your mixed text-generation (50%) + embeddings (50%) steady-state at ~200k qps-equivalent, we recommend a blended pool: 40% A40-class (memory-forward, good for embeddings), 50% H100-accelerated quantized instances for throughput-heavy gen, and 10% T4/RTX-class as burst spots for cheap short bursts. See attached tab "SKU-recommendation".
- Token/sec guidance (approx): H100-quantized (gpt-3-family equivalent): 1.2k-1.8k tokens/sec per GPU depending on kv-cache utilization and batch size; A40 (embedding heavy): 2.5k-4k embeddings/sec (smaller token sizes); T4/RTX: 600-1k tokens/sec for cheap bursts.
- Tail latency: With continuous batching and prefix caching enabled, p95 ~ 60-120ms, p99 ~ 220-380ms for 1k seq lengths on H100-class under steady-state. A40 for embeddings p99 ~ 120ms.
- Burst runway: We provide configurable burst lanes. Without pre-warm, short bursts up to ~2.5x baseline are absorbed by autoscale buffers (subject to pool headroom). For deterministic higher bursts we recommend pre-warmed burst capacity (we can reserve on short-term commitments). Cold-starts for scaled-up GPUs typically add 20-90s to get kernels loaded unless warm pools are allocated.
- Fallbacks: Transparent fallback is supported; the routing layer can shift traffic to a quantized or lower-SKU variant with documented quality delta. We include canary rollouts and automatic fallback policy in the config.
- Billing: Burst beyond committed baseline is billed at an overage rate (per-GPU-hour) or via burst credits if purchased. Commitment tiers reduce unit cost by 15-30% depending on term length.

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute sizing call tomorrow where we walk the attached workbook and pick an initial sku-mix. I'm available 9:30-11:30am PT.

Attaching: redwood_dedicated_sku_matrix_v1.xlsx, SLA-draft-Cyclone-20270519.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime

Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing + SLA questions

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. Two follow-ups before the call:

1) Quality trade-off: if you fall back from H100 quantized to A40 or to a more-quantized variant, do you have quantifiable eval deltas for common tasks (summarization, code, instruction-following)? Even rough BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity deltas would help our ML infra team.
2) Can you confirm whether the cold-start 20-90s applies to both single-GPU allocations and multi-GPU model shards? We run multi-shard models for some of our large agents.

Also we prefer an initial reservation commitment of 6 months with a month-to-month burst top-up — pricing sensitive. Please call out where we can trade latency vs cost (e.g., larger batch windows reduce token cost but increase p95).

Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Ops, Cyclone AI
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cycloneai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing + SLA questions

Elena — adding a few concrete datapoints from our eval lab for the quality and cold-start questions so you have numbers for procurement.

Quality delta (representative): on instruction-following tasks with a Bloom-style 7B baseline vs H100-quantized gpt-family variant, we see average embedding cosine similarity drop of ~0.012 (±0.006) and ROUGE-L relative change ~ -1.8%. For summarization the degradation on 1-bit quantized kernels is typically in the 1-3% ROUGE-L range; extremes depend on prompt engineering. We'll include a short eval pack in the drive link.

Cold-start behavior: For single-GPU model loads in our infra it aligns with Karthik's note (20-90s depending on model size and kernel JIT). For multi-shard large models the cold-start is dominated by model chunk transfer and KV cache allocation — we've measured 45-210s on our lab images for 8+ shard setups if no warm pool is present. If you require <30s scaling, we recommend reserved warm standby capacity or using short-lived pre-warmed nodes.

Also, cost/latency knobs:
- Increase batching window from 10ms to 50ms: token cost down by ~12-18% at the expense of ~15-40ms added p95.
- Aggressive KV caching: reduces token work for many users and lowers cost but requires memory-heavy SKUs (A100/A40).

We can walk these numbers on the call and show the workbook scenario tabs.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — the eval deltas and cold-start ranges are exactly what procurement needs. Two quick items before we lock the 30-minute slot:

- Can you add a recommendation for an initial 6-month commitment SKU mix in the workbook that keeps our 6-month committed spend under $1.2M while still providing 2x burst lane for holiday peaks?
- Please flag any lock-in or migration risk if we later want to shift to a private deployment (VPC) vs hosted Redwood Dedicated. We need that for our legal team.

Proposed call: Thu 20 May 2027, 10:30am PT — available?

Elena
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cycloneai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, procurement@cycloneai.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing + SLA questions

Elena — quick replies inline and we've updated the workbook (tab "6mo-commitment-plan"):

- 6-month recommendation: Blend 52 H100-class, 32 A40-class, 8 T4 burst nodes. That profile hits your steady-state throughput and provides a pre-paid burst credit pool to cover ~1.8-2.0x short bursts. Estimated committed spend (net of enterprise discount) ~ $1.05M for 6 months. See workbook for line-by-line.
- Migration risk: Minimal. Private (VPC) deployments use the same control plane (customer-managed networking) and our model variants and kernel stack are supported across both modes. Migration operational work: data plane IP/networking, private image sync, and KMS key rotation. Contractually we include a migration addendum — no forced vendor lock-in clauses.
- Call confirmed: Thu 20 May 2027 10:30am PT — calendar invite sent from my account.

We've uploaded the updated SKU matrix and a short summary PDF to the drive link in the related_links field. If you'd like, Monica can run a short simulation with your traffic CSV against these SKUs to show expected tail-latency contours.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
